title: Module extension by zero is linear on the unbounded derived category
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the chosen sheaf universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative $A$-algebras on $\mathcal C$, and let $U$ be an object. Write $\mathcal O_U$ for its restriction to the localized ringed site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Use the categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Give all Hom sets the $A$-module structures induced by $A\to\mathcal O$, degreewise on complexes and then by localization [def-weil-linear-category, lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. Let $j_{U!}F=P_F^\#$ be the functorial module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the direct-sum extension presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. On sheaf morphisms $t,t':F\to G$ and $a\in A$, it satisfies $j_{U!}(t+t')=j_{U!}t+j_{U!}t'$ and $j_{U!}(at)=a\,j_{U!}t$. Its termwise functor descends to an additive $A$-linear functor
$$D(j_{U!}):D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_U))\longrightarrow D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$$
[def-weil-linear-functor], which commutes with integer shifts and preserves distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category].

proof.text: Write $c_V:A\to\mathcal O(V)$ for the compatible structural ring maps. For parallel module-sheaf morphisms $t,t':F\to G$, define $(t+t')_V(x)=t_V(x)+t'_V(x)$ and $(at)_V(x)=c_V(a)t_V(x)$. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], these are morphisms: restrictions are semilinear and carry $c_V(a)$ to $c_W(a)$; commutativity of $\mathcal O(V)$ makes $at$ an $\mathcal O(V)$-linear map. The module axioms hold sectionwise, and for composable maps $t,s$, $s_V(c_V(a)t_V(x))=c_V(a)s_V(t_V(x))$ gives bilinearity of composition. Apply this also on $\mathcal C/U$, where $\mathcal O_U(V\to U)=\mathcal O(V)$ by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. These are the $A$-linear structures of [def-weil-linear-category]. Both module categories are abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]: the site is small in the stated universe, and so is its slice.

proof.text: With the sectionwise scalar structures of Step 1, restriction j_U^* is A-linear: evaluation at (V → U) is evaluation at V, and rho_U(V → U) = rho(V). This is a definitional identity on morphisms, using [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Definition of restriction to the localized ringed site, and Lemma extension-by-zero (Tag 03DI).

proof.text: Use the adjunction L = j_U! ⊣ R = j_U^* from [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. For f : X → Y and a ∈ A, apply its injective Hom bijection to L(af) and aL(f). The first image is η_X R(L(af)) = (af)η_Y = a(fη_Y), by unit naturality and bilinearity; the second is η_X R(aL(f)) = a(η_X R(L(f))) = a(fη_Y), by linearity of R and unit naturality. Thus L(af) = aL(f). Additivity is already part of the cited exactness statement. This elementary adjunction calculation replaces the direct-sum and sheafification scalar calculations, without changing the extension functor. This is the existing library lemma CategoryTheory.Adjunction.left_adjoint_linear (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Linear.LinearFunctor), whose proof is exactly this elementary calculation.

source.place: Lemma extension-by-zero (Tag 03DI): the adjunction. The displayed scalar argument is written here by Z7 from unit naturality.

proof.text: The exact functor $j_{U!}$ of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] is precisely the module sheafification $P_F^\#$ with the functorial direct-sum action in its definition; that node assumes an arbitrary localized ringed site, not merely a scheme or finite constant coefficients. Apply [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] to these two abelian module categories and this exact additive functor. It yields the termwise induced unbounded functor $D(j_{U!})$, commuting with integer shifts and preserving distinguished triangles. In particular it is additive. No boundedness or resolution hypothesis is needed for this exact-functor construction.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero and lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); derived.tex Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), implemented by Mathlib ExactFunctor.lean:35-105.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category] applied to the two abelian $A$-linear categories of Step 1, the derived Hom groups have exactly the structures induced by degreewise scalars and localization required in the statement. Apply [lem-cbc-exact-linear-derived-functor] with $R=A$ and $F=j_{U!}$: Step 3 gives its $A$-linearity and Step 4 its exactness. The conclusion is $D(j_{U!})(af)=aD(j_{U!})(f)$ and preservation of sums for every derived morphism, not only for morphisms represented by a single cochain map. Together with Step 4 this proves all the assertions.
